SUMMARY: Track A capstone: task manager on Amazon ECS Fargate
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want to run the task-manager app on ECS Fargate with automated, safe, observable and least-privilege delivery so that I complete the Track A capstone.
DESCRIPTION: Learner backlog for Track A (shared foundation M1 + M2–M8), following the content packs and the Track A capstone brief. All rows start To Do; update STATUS in your own copy as you go. Every AWS resource is created by Terraform; each session ends with terraform destroy in reverse order.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- All 16 Track A capstone requirements met
- Documentation Gate evidence complete in `docs/capstone/`
- Live 30-minute defense passed (75%+ and gate met)

SUMMARY: Set up tools, AWS access and the infra/ folder
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want my tools, AWS identity and Terraform backend settings ready so that every later stack starts from the same setup.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 (Hands-on lab steps 1–2). Install/check Terraform 1.11+, AWS CLI v2, Docker buildx, git, curl, jq. Confirm `aws sts get-caller-identity` and region `ap-southeast-1`. In your gitlab.com project add `infra/backend.hcl` (your state bucket, `use_lockfile = true`, `encrypt = true`) and `infra/env.sh` (`TF_VAR_learner_id`, `TF_VAR_state_bucket`).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `aws sts get-caller-identity` shows the sandbox account
- `aws configure get region` prints `ap-southeast-1`
- `infra/backend.hcl` and `infra/env.sh` are committed, with no secrets in either

SUMMARY: Pin Terraform and create the ECR repositories
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want pinned providers and two ECR repositories so that everyone gets the same behavior and my images have a home.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 (Hands-on lab steps 3–4). In `infra/10-foundation`: `versions.tf` (required_version >= 1.11, aws 6.66.0, random 3.9.1, S3 backend key `dcta/10-foundation.tfstate`, standard `default_tags`), `variables.tf` (region, learner_id, learner_cidr with /32 validation), `ecr.tf` (`dcta-frontend`, `dcta-backend`, IMMUTABLE tags, lifecycle: expire untagged after 1 day, keep last 2 tagged).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Provider versions are exact and `.terraform.lock.hcl` is committed
- `terraform -chdir=infra/10-foundation apply` creates both repositories
- Tags are immutable and the lifecycle policy keeps the last 2 images

SUMMARY: Store the DB password without it ever touching state
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want the database password generated straight into Secrets Manager so that it never appears in Git or any Terraform state file.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 (Hands-on lab step 5). `secrets.tf` in 10-foundation: `ephemeral "random_password"`, `aws_secretsmanager_secret` `dcta/db/credentials` (recovery window 0), `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` with `secret_string_wo` (username `taskadmin` + password) and `secret_string_wo_version`, plus SSM parameter `/dcta/db/name` = `taskdb`.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `terraform state show aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.db` shows no secret string
- No password in Git history
- `/dcta/db/name` exists in Parameter Store

SUMMARY: Prepare the app for AWS (TLS, production frontend, seed)
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want the reference app ready to run on AWS so that it connects to RDS over TLS, fits a small container and gets a fresh schema every session.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 (Hands-on lab step 7). (a) Backend `server.js`: `ssl` option driven by `DB_SSL_CA_PATH`; backend Dockerfile adds the RDS ap-southeast-1 CA bundle. (b) Frontend: multi-stage Dockerfile (node build → `nginx:1.30-alpine`), `REACT_APP_API_URL=/api`, remove the `location /api/` block from `nginx.conf`. (c) `app/database/seed.sql`: re-runnable schema + 3 sample tasks.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Local `docker compose up` still works (DB_SSL_CA_PATH unset)
- Frontend image serves the React build from nginx on port 80
- Running `seed.sql` twice adds no duplicate rows

SUMMARY: Build and push amd64 images tagged with the Git SHA
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want both images in ECR, built for amd64 and tagged with my commit, so that AWS can run them and I always know which code is live.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 (Hands-on lab step 8). Log Docker in with `aws ecr get-login-password`, then `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 -t <registry>/dcta-<app>:<short-sha> --push` for backend and frontend.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `aws ecr describe-images` lists the short commit SHA for both repositories
- Images are linux/amd64
- No `latest` tag is used

SUMMARY: Write the VPC with no NAT Gateway
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want a 2-AZ VPC with public and private subnets so that containers can reach ECR directly and the database stays private.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 Lab exercise item 1. In 10-foundation: VPC across `ap-southeast-1a`/`1b`, 2 public + 2 private subnets, Internet Gateway, public route table, no NAT Gateway, `map_public_ip_on_launch = true` on the public subnets.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- 4 subnets, 2 per AZ
- `describe-nat-gateways` count is 0
- Public subnets assign public IPs on launch

SUMMARY: Chain the security groups and publish the foundation outputs
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want security groups that point at each other and a stable outputs contract so that only my app can reach the database and later stacks can read the foundation.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 Lab exercise items 2–3. `dcta-alb-sg`, `dcta-app-sg`, `dcta-rds-sg`: internet ingress only from `var.learner_cidr`; RDS 5432 only from `dcta-app-sg`; any 0.0.0.0/0 egress carries a `# justification:` comment. Outputs exactly: vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, alb_sg_id, app_sg_id, rds_sg_id, ecr_repository_urls, db_secret_arn, db_name_parameter_arn.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `dcta-rds-sg` ingress references `dcta-app-sg`, with no IP ranges
- No internet-facing 0.0.0.0/0 ingress
- All 9 outputs exist with the exact names

SUMMARY: Create the ephemeral database stack
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want RDS in its own stack that I create and destroy every session so that it only exists while I work and is never reachable from the internet.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 Lab exercise items 4–5. `infra/20-data` (key `dcta/20-data.tfstate`): `terraform_remote_state` of 10-foundation, DB subnet group on the private subnets, `aws_db_instance` `dcta-postgres` (PostgreSQL 17, db.t4g.micro, `password_wo` from the ephemeral secret, not public, no final snapshot), SSM `/dcta/db/host`; output `db_host_parameter_arn`. Destroy and re-apply it with no manual steps.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- RDS is available, `PubliclyAccessible: false`, in the private subnets
- `/dcta/db/host` holds the RDS address
- Destroy + re-apply works with no manual steps
- Failure path: `nc` from your laptop to RDS on 5432 fails

SUMMARY: Create the Track A stack: cluster and execution role
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want an ECS cluster and a narrowly scoped execution role so that ECS can start my containers with only the secrets they need.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M2 (Hands-on lab steps 1–3). `infra/30-track-a`: versions (key `dcta/30-track-a.tfstate`), `remote_state.tf` (foundation + data), `aws_ecs_cluster` `dcta-ecs` (Container Insights off) + capacity providers FARGATE/FARGATE_SPOT, `dcta-ecs-task-execution` role (managed policy + read only `dcta/db/credentials`, `/dcta/db/name`, `/dcta/db/host`).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- No copied IDs — everything comes from `terraform_remote_state`
- Execution role can read only the 1 secret and 2 parameters

SUMMARY: Add the ALB, target groups and seed task
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want one load balancer and a re-runnable seed task so that the app has a single address and a fresh database every session.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M2 (Hands-on lab steps 4–6). `alb.tf`: `dcta-alb`, `dcta-frontend-tg` (80) and `dcta-backend-tg` (3000), `ip` targets, `/health` checks, listener :80 defaulting to the frontend. `seed.tf`: `dcta-db-seed` task running `seed.sql` with `psql`, output `seed_run_command`. Learn the Track A session commands (image-tag exports, apply, seed, reverse destroy).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `alb_dns_name` output exists
- Seed task exits 0; a second run inserts 0 rows

SUMMARY: Write the frontend and backend task definitions
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want task definitions that inject the DB settings safely so that no password is ever in plain environment variables.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M2 Lab exercise items 1–2. Fargate, awsvpc, X86_64, 256 CPU / 512 MiB, images from ECR tagged via `var.frontend_image_tag` / `var.backend_image_tag`. Backend: DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD from the secret JSON keys, DB_HOST/DB_NAME from Parameter Store, `environment` PORT=3000, DB_PORT=5432, DB_SSL_CA_PATH=/app/certs/rds-ca.pem.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Both task definitions: Fargate, X86_64, 256/512, SHA tags
- Nothing sensitive in `environment`

SUMMARY: Run both services on 70% Fargate Spot
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want both services running behind the ALB with a 70/30 Spot split so that the app is live while using low-cost capacity.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M2 Lab exercise items 3–4. `aws_ecs_service` for both: desired_count 1, public subnets, `dcta-app-sg`, `assign_public_ip = true`, matching target group, capacity provider strategy FARGATE_SPOT weight 7 / FARGATE weight 3. Apply, run the seed, open the app via the ALB.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `describe-services` shows both running with the 7/3 strategy
- Backend target is healthy
- The app loads and CRUD works through the ALB

SUMMARY: Route /api/* to the backend and prove it
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want path-based routing on one ALB so that the browser calls the API on the same address as the page.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M3 Lab exercise item 5 + failure proofs. `aws_lb_listener_rule` for `/api/*` → backend target group; default action stays on the frontend. The console is for looking only — no rules created by hand.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `/api/tasks` returns JSON; `/` returns 200
- Failure path: `/api/does-not-exist` returns the Express `Cannot GET` page
- Failure path: with the backend at 0 tasks, `/api/tasks` returns 503 while `/` returns 200

SUMMARY: Week 5 review: run the daily routine end to end
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want one clean apply-to-destroy run so that the daily routine is automatic before Week 6.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, Week 5 Day 5 (capstone timeline). Run the full session: exports, apply 10-foundation → 20-data → 30-track-a, seed, check the app, destroy 30-track-a → 20-data. Save Week 5 evidence in `docs/capstone/`.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Full session runs with no manual fixes
- No ALB or RDS remains after destroy
- Week 5 evidence saved in `docs/capstone/`

SUMMARY: Create the keyless CI role (GitLab OIDC)
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want GitLab CI to log in to AWS without any access key so that no long-lived credential exists anywhere.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M4 (Hands-on lab steps 1–2). `infra/10-foundation/ci.tf`: `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider` for https://gitlab.com, role `dcta-gitlab-ci` trusted only for `project_path:<group>/<project>:ref_type:branch:ref:main` (aud https://gitlab.com), policy limited to your 2 ECR repos, task definitions, your 2 services and PassRole of the task roles to ECS; output `ci_role_arn`. Add `TF_VAR_gitlab_project_path` to env.sh and a protected `AWS_ROLE_ARN` CI/CD variable.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- OIDC provider and role are created by Terraform
- No AWS access key exists for CI
- Role trust is pinned to your project's `main` branch

SUMMARY: Add CI build jobs that push SHA-tagged images
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want every merge to main to build and push both images so that deploys always use an image tied to a commit.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M4 (Hands-on lab step 4). `.gitlab-ci.yml`: `.aws-docker` template (docker:29 + docker:29-dind, `id_tokens` with aud https://gitlab.com, web-identity token file, ECR login), `build-backend-aws` and `build-frontend-aws` with `--platform linux/amd64`, default branch only.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Both build jobs pass on `main`
- The newest ECR tag equals the pushed commit's short SHA

SUMMARY: Deploy from CI with zero downtime and automatic rollback
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want merges to main to roll out without errors and roll back by themselves when broken so that users never see a bad release.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M4 Lab exercise items 1–3 + failure proof. Services: minimum healthy 100%, maximum 200%, circuit breaker with rollback, `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [task_definition, desired_count] }`. CI `deploy` stage: fetch task definition, swap `$IMAGE_TAG`, register, `update-service`, `wait services-stable`.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- A merge to `main` rolls out a new revision
- Deploy job fails if the service isn't stable
- `rollout.log` during a rollout shows only 200
- Failure path: a broken image fails the job, ECS rolls back, and users still see only 200

SUMMARY: Build the CloudWatch dashboard
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want one dashboard with service CPU and ALB metrics so that I can see the app's health at a glance.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M5 (Hands-on lab step 2). `aws_cloudwatch_dashboard` `dcta-ecs`: service CPU for both services (70% line) and ALB RequestCount / HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: - Dashboard `dcta-ecs` exists and shows both widgets

SUMMARY: Ship every container's logs to CloudWatch
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want all container logs in Terraform-managed log groups so that logs survive after tasks stop and don't pile up forever.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M5 Lab exercise item 4. `awslogs` logConfiguration on both containers; `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` `/dcta/ecs/frontend` and `/dcta/ecs/backend` with retention of 7 days or less.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `aws logs tail /dcta/ecs/backend` shows request logs
- Both log groups have retention ≤ 7 days

SUMMARY: Auto-scale the backend on CPU and prove it
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want the backend to grow from 1 to 3 tasks at 70% CPU so that it handles load without me touching it.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M5 Lab exercise items 5–6. `aws_appautoscaling_target` (1–3) and a target-tracking policy on ECSServiceAverageCPUUtilization = 70. Run a 5-minute `ab` load test.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Scaling activities show 1 → 3 and back to 1
- With 3 tasks, `describe-tasks` shows both FARGATE_SPOT and FARGATE
- Dashboard screenshot saved

SUMMARY: Add the alternate target group and ECS infrastructure role
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want the pieces ECS needs for blue/green so that a new backend version can start beside the old one.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M6 (Hands-on lab step 1). `dcta-backend-tg-alt` (3000, `/health`) and role `dcta-ecs-infra-lb` trusted by ecs.amazonaws.com with AmazonECSInfrastructureRolePolicyForLoadBalancers.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: - Alternate target group and infrastructure role exist

SUMMARY: Switch the backend to blue/green
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want blue/green releases for the backend so that I can test a new version privately and switch back instantly.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M6 Lab exercise items 1–2. Test listener rule (priority below the /api/* rule) matching /api/* AND header `X-Deploy-Stage: test` → alternate TG; `ignore_changes = [action]` on both rules; backend service `strategy = "BLUE_GREEN"`, 5-minute bake, advanced_configuration (alternate TG, production rule, test rule, infra role); ignore `load_balancer`. Frontend stays rolling.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Backend uses BLUE_GREEN with a 5-minute bake; frontend is still rolling
- `terraform plan` after a deployment shows no rule changes

SUMMARY: Run a blue/green deploy and a rollback
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want to see a blue/green release and a rollback work end to end so that I can rely on them at the defense.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M6 Lab exercise item 3 + failure proof. Merge a visible backend change; compare the normal route with `curl -H 'X-Deploy-Stage: test'`; watch the production switch. Start a second deployment and run `stop-service-deployment --stop-type ROLLBACK` during bake time.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Test route returned the new version while the normal route was still old
- After the switch the normal route serves the new version
- Failure path: rollback during bake time points the production rule back at the original target group

SUMMARY: Create least-privilege task roles
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want each service to have its own minimal AWS identity so that a compromised container can do almost nothing.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M7 Lab exercise item 4. `dcta-backend-task`: only secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the DB secret and ssm:GetParameter(s) on `/dcta/db/host` and `/dcta/db/name`. `dcta-frontend-task`: no permissions. Set `task_role_arn` on both task definitions.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Each service has its own task role
- Backend role is scoped to the 1 secret and 2 parameters
- The app still works end to end

SUMMARY: Prove least privilege with the IAM probe
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want a repeatable test that shows which calls are denied so that least privilege is proven, not just claimed.
DESCRIPTION: Track A, M7 (Hands-on lab probe task + Lab exercise item 5). `dcta-iam-probe` task (aws-cli 2.37.4) run with `--overrides taskRoleArn` for the backend role, then the frontend role. Print secret names only, never values.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Backend role: 2 allowed calls print names
- Failure path: another secret, `list-secrets` and `s3 ls` are AccessDenied
- Failure path: frontend role is denied everything

SUMMARY: Complete the capstone documentation
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want all my evidence in one place so that I pass the Documentation Gate.
DESCRIPTION: Track A capstone Documentation section. In `docs/capstone/`: apply/destroy output for 10-foundation, 20-data, 30-track-a; failed `nc`; NAT count; routing and 503 tests; rollout.log summary; circuit-breaker rollback; blue/green and rollback evidence; IAM probe logs; scaling activities, Spot mix and dashboard screenshot; teardown proof; own-words explanation of the daily apply/destroy order.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Every evidence item in the capstone spec's Documentation list is present and real
- Own-words explanation of the apply/destroy order is included

SUMMARY: Rehearse the 30-minute defense
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want a practiced run-through so that the live defense fits in 30 minutes.
DESCRIPTION: Track A capstone (Day 10 prep). Follow the rubric agenda: session start, commit → blue/green, load test → scaling, IAM probe, teardown, then Q&A and a live destructive test. Prepare answers to the rubric's "why" questions.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- A full run-through fits in 30 minutes, including Q&A time
- You can answer each of the rubric's Track A "why" questions

SUMMARY: Deliver the live 30-minute defense and tear everything down
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want to demonstrate the whole system live and leave nothing running so that I complete Track A.
DESCRIPTION: Track A capstone, M8. Live 30-minute defense per the rubric, then `terraform destroy` on 30-track-a → 20-data and confirm no load balancer remains. Last day only: deregister and delete the CI-registered `dcta-*` task definition revisions, then destroy 10-foundation.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defense completed within 30 minutes
- `describe-load-balancers` returns 0 and no NAT Gateway exists
- Last day: no `dcta-*` task definitions remain and 10-foundation is destroyed
